one_paragraph_summary: Columbia University students in NYC ignited pro-Palestinian rallies that within days spread to at least thirty other US universities and then to France, the United Kingdom, Norway, Australia, and elsewhere -- joining longer-running demonstrations in Arab and Muslim countries. CJ believes -- IMHO -- that the headline-grabbing US student rallies influenced US pressure on Israel to temper its Gaza attacks and to pursue a ceasefire coupled with hostage release. Inevitably and unfortunately, 'outside actors' infiltrated the ranks, shifting the events from free expression to vandalism and violence, and the NYC police responded 'in full force, shields, sticks, and arms.' The Columbia students remind him of his own days as president of the Far Eastern University Central Student Organization (FEUCSO) and of the National Union of Students of the Philippines (NUSP), when he 'led the birth of campus activism here,' battling alongside the UP Student Council under Fernando Lagua, the UP 'Collegian' under editor-in-chief Homobono Adaza, and the UP Student Catholic Action under Emmanuel Soriano. He confesses that, as an impoverished youth who could not study without scholarships and who 'had to hawk newspapers and textbooks,' he was 'enamored by Karl Marx's cry of From each according to his ability, and to each according to his needs.' Two people dissuaded him. First, Fr. Michael Nolan, FEU chaplain and Manila SCA spiritual director, taught him simple catechesis and challenged him to study the actual economic reality of Red China and Russia -- proving communism 'theoretically attractive' but 'not implementable.' Second, Elenita 'Leni' Carpio, editor of the 'Scholastican' and aspiring Benedictine nun, met him as an 'accidental' seatmate on a ten-hour Manila-to-Naga train ride to an NUSP seminar; over three years of conversations she 'converted' him into a 'willing soldier of Christ,' and married him to the 'chagrin of the St. Scho nuns who expected her to join them in blessed singlehood.' Pope John Paul II later named him to the Pontifical Council for the Laity in the Vatican for the 1996-2002 term, succeeding Ambassador Henrietta 'Tita' de Villa. CJ closes with the Philippine arc: student activism here owes its origin to Wenceslao Q. Vinzons (resisting the Japanese invasion in 1941); the late-1950s peacetime activism bloomed into the 1970 First Quarter Storm led by NUSP's Edgar Jopson, UP's Jerry Barican, and Kabataang Makabayan's Jose Ma. Sison and Satur Ocampo -- Jan. 26 to March 17, 1970, against Marcos Sr. While present-day Filipino student leaders are 'not yet' engaged with the Israel-Hamas war, Russia-Ukraine war, or West Philippine Sea tensions, CJ expects they will engage when they realize 'there is no dispute so remote and so misunderstood they would not take a stand on.'
